newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open steady to firmer.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open mostly steady to firmer Monday, with gold and silver expected to continue to drift into summer within current ranges and platinum group metals continuing to consolidate while waiting for the return of Russian exports.
COMEX August gold was called unchanged to up $0.20 from Friday's finish of $343.10 an ounce after trading from $342.90 to $343.50 on ACCESS.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $340.90/$341.40 early against the London morning fix of $340.95.
In New York Friday, spot gold ended quoted at $340.80/$341.30.
The market was ignoring a new Federal Reserve study arguing the U.S. and other governments should sell off their gold reserves to reap a gain of around $370 billion.
But the study by Fed economist Dale Henderson and American university economists was not seen reflecting the views of the Fed or Chairman Greenspan.

Meanwhile, Jean-Pierre Patat of the French central bank told delgates at the Financial Times annual gold conference in Prague Monday that several European central banks which had recently sold some gold reserves no longer feel there is an advantage in selling more.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks fell 9,271 ounces Friday to 838,963 ounces. COMEX silver stocks fell 3,522,805 ounces to 194,490,662 ounces.
COMEX July silver was called unchanged to up 0.5 cent from Friday's close of $4.675.
NYMEX July platinum was called unchanged to up $1.00 from the previous close of $426.30, with NYMEX September palladium called unchanged to down $1.00 from Friday's finish of $188.40.
Over the weekend, Japanese traders reported a visit by officials of U.S. fund Tiger Management to Japan, seeking to sell some of the palladium stockpile it has built up.
